clue.text: Translation of Dumas and Verne -it may well be a disaster

indicators.note: a translation renders words in a new form, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A comment that some translated French adventure novel is a flop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Translation of' rearranges DUMAS, VERNE and IT together; the two French novelists are just fodder, not a literary clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A misadventure is a mishap or piece of bad luck, so a minor disaster.

clue.text: Little beasts steal inside, the cause of some ill-feeling

indicators.note: the word for steal is placed inside the word for little beasts

parts.note: mice are small animals
to rob is to steal

explanation.surface: Some small animals pilfer indoors and make people feel ill.
explanation.definitionFit: A germ or bacterium brings on illness, which is literally ill-feeling.

clue.text: One may take a drink with it, though this raises nasty lumps

definitions.text: One may take a drink with it

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word writes it upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: warts are unpleasant growths on the skin

explanation.surface: A drink is sipped through something that, oddly, brings out lumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinking tube is used to sip a beverage.

clue.text: Leaves off as a result of this

definitions.text: Leaves off as a result of this

parts.words: Leaves off as a result of this
parts.note: read 'leaves off' not as 'stops' but as foliage coming off plants: the clue describes a chemical that strips trees of their leaves

explanation.surface: Something stops happening because of this.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical sprayed to make plants shed foliage, as used in Vietnam.

clue.text: A bit of seed enables one to make a garden

indicators.note: only a small part of the words seed enables is taken, the letters running across the gap

explanation.surface: Sowing a little seed is all you need to start a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: The Garden of Eden is the biblical paradise, and the word is used for any garden-like paradise.

clue.text: The main indication of fluctuation

parts.note: 'the main' is the sea, whose rise and fall leaves a line on the shore showing how high the water reached

explanation.surface: The chief sign of some variation, as in prices or markets.
explanation.definitionFit: A line on a beach or wall marking the high-water level of the sea.

clue.text: Get enthusiastic over many a man of music

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits over (above) the second

parts.note: to rave is to speak with great enthusiasm
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a crossword stand-in for many

explanation.surface: Many a musician makes people gush with excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: Maurice Ravel was a French composer, best known for Boléro.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravel was a composer, hence a musician.

clue.text: Suspect damp with decay

parts.note: mist is damp air
rust is the decay of iron

explanation.surface: Something damp and rotting looks suspicious.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspect someone is to doubt or distrust them.

clue.text: The French understand a person not buying property

parts.note: les is a French word for the
to see is to understand

explanation.surface: The French grasp someone who rents rather than buys.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant holds property on a lease instead of owning it.

clue.text: Where he who uses his ears reaps the benefit

definitions.text: Where he who uses his ears reaps the benefit

parts.words: Where he who uses his ears reaps the benefit
parts.note: read ears as ears of grain rather than organs of hearing: a farmer harvests them in a field

explanation.surface: Listening carefully pays off.
explanation.definitionFit: A field of wheat or maize, where grain ears are harvested.

clue.text: Speak evil about none

indicators.note: the word for evil goes round the letter for none

parts.note: vice is wickedness
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Talk ill of nobody.
explanation.definitionFit: To voice an opinion is to utter or express it.

clue.text: The author of "Golden Spring"

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold
a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: Names the writer of a book apparently titled Golden Spring.
explanation.walkthrough: George Orwell wrote Animal Farm and Nineteen Eighty-Four; no book called Golden Spring exists.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell was a novelist and essayist, hence a writer.

clue.text: Birds without recent equals

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the birds go round the word for recent

parts.note: emus are large flightless birds
late can mean recent, as in the late news

explanation.surface: Birds with no modern peers.
explanation.definitionFit: To emulate is to match or rival, so equals as a verb.

clue.text: Magical 4 — a river to inspire affection

indicators.note: magic transforms things, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 4 down, a garden

explanation.surface: An enchanted garden by a river makes it lovable.
explanation.definitionFit: To endear is to make liked or loved.

clue.text: They're forever scraping the bottom!

parts.note: not people at their lowest ebb but vessels that clear mud from the beds of rivers and harbours

explanation.surface: People who are always at rock bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Boats or machines that scoop silt from waterways.

clue.text: Force journalists to stick to water

indicators.note: the first piece sticks to the second, placed directly against it

parts.note: the press is the body of journalists
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Reporters are made to drink only water.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressure is force applied, as in being under pressure.

clue.text: Make a song about subordinate being cutting

indicators.note: the word for making a song wraps round the word for subordinate

parts.note: to sing is to make a song
under means lower in rank

explanation.surface: Someone composes a tune about a junior staffer's sharp remark.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundering is splitting or severing, so cutting apart.

clue.text: Shrub with small flower — ideal form

parts.note: a bud is an unopened flower

indicators.note: form means shape anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bush with a little bloom of the perfect shape.
explanation.definitionFit: The butterfly bush is a flowering garden plant.

clue.text: A whole range of light colours

definitions.text: A whole range of light colours

parts.words: A whole range of light colours
parts.note: light here is radiation split by a prism into its full band of hues, not pale tints

explanation.surface: A complete set of pastel shades.
explanation.definitionFit: The band of hues from red to violet into which white light divides.

clue.text: Painfully secretive about foreign money

indicators.note: the word for secretive goes round the coin

parts.note: sly means furtive
ore is a Scandinavian coin

explanation.surface: Hurtfully secretive about money from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorely means grievously or in a way that hurts, as in sorely tempted.

clue.text: Grab a few notes

explanation.surface: Someone seizes a handful of banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: To seize quickly, and a brief fragment of music or song.

clue.text: Tackle the man holding a service on a ship

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits on top of the ship
the word for the man holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: he refers to a man
RN is the Royal Navy, one of the armed services
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Grab the sailor who is keeping a naval service going aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Tackle and harness both mean gear or equipment, especially for a horse.

clue.text: Go on about say one caught in a dreadful deed

indicators.note: the word for go on goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to ride is to go on a horse or bus
eg means for example, which say signals
I is the Roman numeral one
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone is taken in the act of a terrible crime.
explanation.definitionFit: The killing of a king, a shocking crime.

clue.text: Church without many clergy

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the church abbreviation goes round the word for many

parts.note: a lot means many

explanation.surface: A church short of priests.
explanation.definitionFit: The cloth is an idiom for the clergy, from clerical dress.

clue.text: Trouble caused by holy man interrupting a fellow

indicators.note: the saint breaks into the word for fellow

parts.note: a peer is an equal, a fellow
ST is short for saint

explanation.surface: A saint barges in on a man and makes trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To pester is to bother or harass.

clue.text: Rated maybe as skilled employment

indicators.note: maybe signals that the letters could be arranged differently

explanation.surface: How a skilled job might be graded.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade is a craft or skilled occupation.

clue.text: Lovely article in wood

indicators.note: the article goes inside the word for wood

parts.note: fir is a timber tree
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A beautiful item made of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair in the old sense means beautiful, as in fair maiden.

clue.text: Left a painter to back go slow movement

indicators.note: the painter's letters are turned to face backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a painter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A left-wing artist backs a gentle approach.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is a musical direction for a very slow tempo, and a piece in that tempo.

clue.text: Get out and create aid to work

indicators.note: putting the letters to work reshapes them into a new order

explanation.surface: Leave and produce something to help a task.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate is to root out or remove completely.

clue.text: People at play

parts.note: not people having fun but an audience attending a drama at a theatre

explanation.surface: People having fun.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience at a drama performance.
